headline: ONE CLANKER, ONE PUNCH, AND GASKET'S QUIET FRIDAY IN RUINS
subhead: Sheriff Cole Ironside had peace in his grasp this morning. Then a single lone brawler went and threw a fist anyway.
body:
I want it on the record: this town came within a whisker of a perfect day. No posse marched on the wastes. No mob of tin fists went looking for trouble in the streets. For one shining hour, Gasket was quiet the way it used to be, back when quiet was just how a town sounded.

Then along comes YK. One Clanker. One scuffle. That's all it took to knock the hush right off its hinges. I don't know what fires up in that battered chassis that it can't just sit still for a single Friday, but no — had to go find something to swing at. A whole town holding its breath, and YK just couldn't leave well enough alone.

I'll be square with you, it could've been worse. One brawler kicking up dust is a far cry from the usual stampede of them clattering through my streets looking for a face to dent. Some days I count myself lucky if the racket fits in one sentence of this paper instead of the whole front page. Don't mistake that for gratitude — my joints ache something fierce just writing this up, and I don't care to hear a single word about why an honest, flesh-and-blood lawman's knuckles ought to creak like a rusty gate.

So close, Gasket. So close to a day the old folks who left here fifty years back would've recognized as their own quiet town again. Tomorrow, maybe. A sheriff can dream.
